items.title: Vestland's RM2bil order book to drive earnings growth: Kenanga Research
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd is expected to post earnings of RM49.4 million and RM77.5 million in the financial year 2026 (FY26) and FY27, respectively, backed by its outstanding order book and tender book. Kenanga Research said the company has an order book of RM2 billion and a tender book of RM5 billion. However, profit margins are expected to rebound moving forward, driven by accelerated cash collection cycles from public infrastructure contracts, a superior margin mix for public sector work versus private projects and a rising share of public sector jobs.

items.title: Melaka polls: Give young candidates a chance to prove their worth, says Adam Adli
items.summary: MELAKA: Young people should not be deemed too inexperienced to contest elections when political parties have long relied on them to carry out much of their campaign work, acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said He said it was unfair to question the suitability of young candidates based solely on their age when they were often the backbone of election campaigns. "But when it comes to becoming candidates, suddenly they are considered too young. Adam Adli, who is also deputy higher education minister, was responding to questions on whether PH's younger candidates could convince older voters who remained sceptical about their experience and capabilities.

items.title: Good service doesn't exempt public officers from the law, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Public officers who demonstrate good performance and contribute to the country deserve recognition but are not exempt from the rule of law, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said no one should be exempt from legal obligations, regardless of their service record or contributions, and that the rule of law must always be respected and upheld. Responding to questions about the action taken against Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, Anwar said the matter stemmed from a police report and must be investigated in accordance with established procedures.

items.title: Man charged with murder of 68-year-old Felda settler in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Nov 3 — A 35-year-old man was charged at the Pengerang Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of an elderly settler at Felda Lok Heng Selatan last month. The accused, Muhammad Iskandar Sentot, nodded to indicate that he understood the charge after it was read out before Magistrate Hidayatul Syuhada Shamsudin. According to the charge sheet, Muhammad Iskandar allegedly murdered Mohd Ariff Md Yusoff, 68, in front of a house at Block 2, Jalan Bersatu, Felda Lok Heng Selatan, Pengerang, at 7.20pm on October 26.

items.title: Immigration steps up 3 operations to curb employment of undocumented migrants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is carrying out three targeted operations to curb the presence of undocumented migrants in the employment sector and prevent their involvement in unauthorised business activities. The operations, known as Op Hijau, Op Jaja and Op Belanja, are being conducted by the Home Ministry and the Immigration Department. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government continued to conduct enforcement operations to address the presence of foreigners, particularly undocumented migrants.

items.title: Rafizi at Bukit Aman over RM9.5mil bribery allegation against Ramanan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli arrived at Bukit Aman today to have his statement recorded over allegations that PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan received a RM9.5 million bribe in connection with the corporate mafia issue. Rafizi, who arrived around 11am, briefly spoke to reporters outside the federal police headquarters before entering the compound to assist in investigations. He confirmed that police had summoned him to give a statement over remarks he made during a speech in Selayang on Oct 20.

items.title: Tanjung Bungah residents demand halt to Sore Thumb development
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Tanjung Bungah residents staged a demonstration outside the state legislative assembly building today, demanding that the government immediately halt a developer's plans to alter the natural Sore Thumb promontory. Residents warned that extensive engineering works on natural terrain could invite disaster. Tanjung Bungah Residents' Association (TBRA) chairman Zulfikar Aziz criticised the developer's plans to reduce the lush hill from 18m to six metres, remove mature vegetation and build a massive concrete seawall along the public shoreline.

items.title: Binance reaffirms commitment to Malaysia return, absorbs US$6.3bil impact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Binance has reiterated its commitment to engaging with Malaysian regulators over a potential licensed return to the country and absorbing the financial impact of a recent US$6.3 billion (RM25.6 billion) security breach. This comes more than five years after the SC ordered Binance to cease operations in Malaysia in 2021. Responding to Business Times' queries, a Binance spokesperson said the company remained committed to working constructively with both regulators.

items.title: AI firm Anthropic posts US$104bil losses ahead of IPO
items.summary: Meanwhile, its revenue soared to US$33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up from US$2.5 billion in the same period last year. In the first three quarters of 2025, losses totalled US$25 billion. In the updated prospectus, Anthropic included its financial results for the third quarter, reporting a loss of US$23.3 billion on revenue of US$17 billion.

items.title: Dialog's RM200mil tank expansion to bolster recurring income
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts view Dialog Group Bhd's latest expansion of its petroleum product storage capacity in Tanjung Langsat, Johor, positively, saying it will strengthen the group's recurring income base and support its midstream growth prospects. Dialog announced an additional 100,000 cubic metres (cbm) storage capacity at its wholly owned Dialog Terminals Langsat 3 (DTL3), with completion targeted by mid-2029. The expansion, estimated to cost up to RM200 million, will increase DTL3's capacity by 26 per cent to 480,000 cbm from 380,000 cbm currently, bringing Dialog's total storage capacity at Tanjung Langsat to more than 1.1 million cbm.

items.title: STR, Sara effectiveness should be measured by overall benefits
items.summary: Economist Professor Emeritus Dr Barjoyai Bardai of the Malaysia University of Science and Technology (MUST) said the increase in the combined allocation for STR and SARA to RM16 billion next year should be assessed based on the overall benefits to recipients, including how well the assistance meets their basic needs and improves their purchasing power. "The success of STR and SARA in 2027 should not be judged simply by whether cash assistance has increased or decreased. Barjoyai said the combination of cash assistance and targeted support for basic necessities allowed recipients to meet different household needs, with STR providing the flexibility to pay utility bills, transport costs and children's education expenses, while SARA helped cover the cost of essential goods.

items.title: Melaka polls: Adly admits Bukit Katil 'a challenge', defends performance amid criticism
items.summary: MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan chairman Adly Zahari has acknowledged that retaining the Bukit Katil seat would be challenging due to the cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional. He said voters should assess his performance based on the initiatives and development projects delivered during his tenure, rather than political alignments alone. He said Bukit Katil had also benefited from development projects channelled through the Defence Ministry's Civil-Military Cooperation (CIMIC) programme.

items.title: Armed syndicates make migrant-smuggling crackdown harder, says MMEA chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Syndicates smuggling illegal immigrants into the country are believed to be arming themselves with pistols and rifles to protect their operations and confront enforcement personnel attempting to foil their activities in Malaysian waters. This has made efforts by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) to curb the smuggling increasingly challenging, as the syndicates are believed to be prepared to use force to prevent their routes and operations from being disrupted. MMEA director-general Admiral (Maritime) Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah said operations to curb the activities were increasingly challenging, not only because of the syndicates' constantly changing tactics but also the possibility that they possessed firearms to protect their operations and evade enforcement.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 3, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened on a choppy note today, fluctuating between positive and negative territory before edging higher, in line with the mixed performance on Wall Street overnight. The benchmark index opened 1.25 points higher at 1,620.76. Trading is expected to remain muted ahead of the US midterm elections later today, with the index likely to trend between 1,615 and 1,625.

items.title: JS-SEZ investment pipeline hits RM88.83bil, 12,796 jobs linked to projects
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) has attracted RM88.83 billion in approved investments, with RM40.3 billion already implemented. The overall investment pipeline is expected to generate 28,755 potential employment opportunities, according to a joint statement issued after the inaugural Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee (JSCMC) meeting in Singapore yesterday. The meeting , co-chaired by Malaysia's Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir and Singapore's Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat, marked a shift towards closer ministerial oversight of the zone's implementation, investment realisation and supporting infrastructure.

items.title: Melaka election: PH open to supporters backing Bersatu candidates
items.summary: MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan has no objection if its supporters vote for Bersatu candidates in constituencies not contested by the coalition in the election. Its chairman, Adly Zahari, said although there was no formal cooperation between PH and Bersatu, the approach taken in this election was aimed at minimising clashes with the party led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, thereby creating room for such support. He said PH also hoped Bersatu would adopt a similar approach by supporting PH candidates in constituencies contested by the coalition.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar warns Malaysia a cyberattack target, orders top-level briefings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is among the countries considered potential targets of cyberattacks, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat today. "Malaysia is certainly among those considered a target," he said. Anwar said the government was also monitoring developments involving the Middle East conflict, Yemen and the Red Sea.

items.title: US signals progress in talks with Iran to avert renewed war
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Monday signaled progress in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Teheran said "intensive" exchanges were underway while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions. He added that "Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible." Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect talks with Washington were taking place via mediators.

items.title: Rining's dedication keeps Lun Bawang musical tapi tradition alive
items.summary: With a cup of black coffee and reggae music playing softly in the background, the 53-year-old musician retreats to his backyard workshop to craft the tapi or tapik, a traditional two-stringed instrument of Sarawak's Lun Bawang community. Originally from the Ba'kelalan highlands, Rining is among the few remaining tapi makers in Malaysia, dedicating his late-night hours to preserving an ancestral craft through intricate carvings on pulai wood, locally known as pelai . Rining said making a tapi involves 10 main stages, from cutting and shaping the wood to intricate carving and smoke treatment.

items.title: Rafizi summoned to Bukit Aman over ‘corporate mafia’ remarks, cancels Melaka campaign event
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said he has been summoned to Bukit Aman today to give a statement over remarks concerning an alleged corporate mafia and a RM9.5 million payment linked to PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. Rafizi alleged that the PKR-led government was using the same legal provisions previously invoked against him to intimidate him whenever he raised allegations concerning the purported corporate mafia and Ramanan. Rafizi said he had initiated legal action against Ramanan over the dispute, having previously challenged him to pursue the matter in court.

items.title: Azman pledges to bring federal initiatives to Paya Rumput
items.summary: TANGGA BATU: Bridging the gap between federal policies and the everyday needs of residents is central to Datuk Azman Abidin's campaign pitch in Paya Rumput. The Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate said feedback gathered during his early campaign walkabouts highlighted several pressing local concerns, particularly the rising cost of living, ageing school infrastructure and job opportunities for youths, which he said required closer alignment with national initiatives. He said that while basic infrastructure and flood-related issues were frequently raised, household expenses remained the biggest concern among residents.

items.title: Mexican investigators raid storage unit rented by Meghan's father Thomas Markle
items.summary: TIJUANA: Mexican authorities raided a storage unit rented by Meghan Markle's estranged father as part of an ongoing investigation into alleged child sex abuse material, the state prosecutor's office told AFP on Monday. Last week, Philippine police said they were investigating a laptop found alongside images of child abuse at a former home of Thomas Markle, whose daughter is married to Britain's Prince Harry. The prosecutor's office of Mexico's Baja California state said Monday it had received an anonymous tip about the existence of child sex abuse material in a storage unit rented by Thomas Markle.

items.title: Falling birth rates no barrier to Sunway's paediatric ambitions: HLIB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd continues to expand its paediatric services at Sunway Medical Centre in Bandar Sunway, despite declining birth rates in the Klang Valley. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said the expansion was supported y two factors, namely rising healthcare spending per child, underpinned by higher household incomes, and potential for long-term patient retention. HLIB said Sunway Medical Centre's current paediatric capabilities reflect about three years of substantial investment in specialised human capital, dedicated facilities and subspeciality development.

items.title: US midterms could weaken Trump's grip on power as Democrats target Congress
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's tumultuous second presidency Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump's legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

items.title: Malaysia's manufacturing sector to support economic growth in Q4: MBSB IB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's manufacturing sector is expected to continue supporting industrial production and overall economic growth in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q4 2026), according to MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB). "The latest PMI reading signals continued growth in industrial production and overall economic activity in Q4 2026," it said. The investment bank said stronger demand had encouraged firms to increase purchasing activity and sustain employment growth for a third consecutive month.

items.title: Road ban stays on e-scooters, but trial findings will shape upcoming laws, says MOT
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Micromobility vehicles such as e-scooters remain strictly prohibited on all public roads for now, but findings from controlled sandbox trials will shape an upcoming comprehensive regulatory framework, the Transport Ministry told Parliament. “However, their use must be implemented in a controlled manner, taking into account road conditions, traffic speeds, user safety and the suitability of infrastructure,” the ministry said. Under the Road Traffic Rules (Prohibition of Use of Certain Micromobility Vehicles) 2021, mopeds, Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs), and Personal Mobility Aids (PMAs) face a blanket ban across public roads nationwide.

items.title: No new extradition request received for Zakir Naik, Home Ministry confirms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The government previously opted not to extradite preacher Dr Zakir Naik to India and has given no commitment to do so, the Home Ministry told the Dewan Rakyat, adding that it has received no new extradition request. The ministry said India’s formal extradition request for Zakir was received on Jan 19, 2018. “The Government of Malaysia has decided not to extradite Dr Zakir Naik to India.

items.title: SD Guthrie's yield drive could unlock RM482m annual profit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SD Guthrie Bhd's ambition to raise plantation oil yields by one tonne per hectare by 2029 could potentially lift its annual net profit by RM482 million, providing a significant earnings growth opportunity beyond fluctuations in crude palm oil (CPO) prices. CIMB Securities said the strategy, outlined by SD Guthrie president and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad in a recent interview with The Edge, could form the basis of the group's forthcoming Value-Up plan. CIMB Securities views upstream productivity improvements as the group's strongest potential catalyst for sustainable earnings growth and a valuation re-rating, followed by land monetisation and higher-value downstream expansion.

items.title: Home Ministry: Putrajaya open to RCI on ‘corporate mafia’ claims if solid grounds established
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The federal government has not dismissed the possibility of convening a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into allegations of a “corporate mafia”, but maintains that this requires a demonstrated need and clearly defined terms of reference, the Home Ministry told the Dewan Rakyat. The ministry said this in a written reply to Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong, who pressed the government on the progress of police investigations, whether identified syndicate masterminds would face prosecution, and whether Putrajaya was prepared to establish an RCI to examine regulatory abuse. To investigate the claims, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) initiated Op Viking through Bukit Aman's Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Team, opening formal investigation papers on October 14, 2025, under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.

items.title: Oil rises after report of US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
items.summary: Brent crude futures rose 48 US cents, or 0.5 per cent, to US$105.25 a barrel by 0104 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 47 US cents, or 0.5 per cent, at US$96.93 a barrel. Brent crude futures settled US$8.66, or 7.63 per cent, lower at US$104.77 a barrel on Monday. The United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia sees choppy start amid mixed Wall Street cues
items.summary: The benchmark index opened 1.25 points higher at 1,620.76. Among the heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose six sen to RM10.04, Public Bank added two sen to RM4.81, and CIMB bagged four sen to RM6.96. In active trade, GIIB and Datasonic were half a sen higher at 50.5 sen and 27 sen, respectively, and AirAsia improved 3.5 sen to 48 sen. Nationgate fell nine sen to RM1.97, and Ni Hsin was half a sen lower at 33.5 sen. Nestle led the top gainers, gaining 42 sen to RM96.54, while Hong Leong Bank rose 20 sen to RM21.38, RHB Bank gained 17 sen to RM7.67, AMMB soared 15 sen to RM6.42, and United Plantations climbed 10 sen to RM29.40.

items.title: Oracle taps investors for US$20bil to finance AI expansion
items.summary: NEW YORK: Oracle plans to raise US$20 billion through bond and share sales, regulatory filings showed on Monday, as the software giant taps investors to fund its costly AI and cloud infrastructure build-out. Oracle had US$125.34 billion in notes payable and other borrowings, as of August 31, compared with fiscal 2026 revenue of US$67.36 billion. It expects revenue to exceed US$225 billion and adjusted earnings to top US$21 per share in fiscal 2030.

items.title: Singapore's Grab lifts 2026 forecasts on strong ride-hailing, delivery demand
items.summary: Grab, Southeast Asia's biggest ride-hailing and delivery firm, now expects 2026 revenue between US$4.15 billion and US$4.20 billion, up from the previous forecast range of US$4.10 billion to US$4.15 billion. It projected annual EBITDA of US$790 million to US$800 million, versus US$720 million to US$740 million earlier. Grab's third-quarter revenue rose 27 per cent to US$1.11 billion, beating analysts' estimates of US$1.07 billion, per LSEG-compiled data.

items.title: Govt open to RCI on corporate mafia issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has not ruled out setting up a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) to address the corporate mafia issue in the country. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government believes it should assess whether there is justification to expand the investigation, including identifying specific areas that require further scrutiny. Saifuddin said police, through Bukit Aman's Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Team, launched Op Viking following information and intelligence relating to money laundering activities.

items.title: The German Makkabi sports club where Muslims outnumber Jews
items.summary: FRANKFURT, (Germany): When they sweat it out at a big German sports club, Jewish, Muslim and other athletes are also sending a strong signal against rising antisemitism, the head of Makkabi Frankfurt told AFP. Founded in 1965 and named after the Maccabee rebel Jewish warriors that fought the Seleucid Greek Empire, the club was set up for Jews in and around Frankfurt to have somewhere to play sport safely, before later opening up to all, club president Alon Meyer said. "It is a Jewish sports club, set up to create a safe space for our Jewish fellow citizens in Frankfurt and the surrounding area, for them to take part in sport without fear," he said.

items.title: Johor’s data centre surge unsettles Iskandar Puteri residents, some consider selling homes
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — Johor’s rapid expansion of data centres has reportedly raised concerns among residents in Iskandar Puteri over noise, environmental conditions and the potential impact of nearby infrastructure on property values. According to Singapore’s The Straits Times , some homeowners are considering selling their properties following the construction of data centres and high-voltage transmission towers near residential neighbourhoods. Among them is finance manager Lee Shi Qing, 38, who reportedly put her RM1 million terraced house in Eco Botanic up for sale after construction began on a nearby 64-megawatt data centre by TM Nxera, a joint venture involving Telekom Malaysia and Singtel’s Nxera.

items.title: Govt to consider proposed Child Act amendments addressing indefinite detention of young offenders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The government is finalising the draft Children (Amendment) Bill 2026 for submission to the Cabinet for consideration, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M Kulasegaran. He said the amendments aimed to improve Section 97 of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611) following the abolition of mandatory death sentences and life imprisonment in 2023 and seek to establish a more proportionate sentencing approach and eliminate indefinite imprisonment of juvenile offenders without a specified detention period. Kulasegaran said the findings of the review had led to the Cabinet’s agreement on Sept 30 to four policy decisions concerning the proposed amendments to Section 97 of Act 611.

items.title: Anwar, Johari-led trade missions generate RM59.5b in potential investments, says Miti
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Fourteen official visits and trade and investment missions led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani were carried out through the country’s trade and investment agencies from 2025 to September 2026. Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said the missions were undertaken through the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) and the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE), generating potential investments of RM59.5 billion. It added that markets which recorded double-digit growth included Namibia (up 426.1 per cent), Angola (55.6 per cent), Brazil (41.0 per cent), Tanzania (35.9 per cent), Ethiopia (28.5 per cent) and Kenya (11.6 per cent).

items.title: GOF arrests 1,733 people, seizes RM82.56m worth of goods in cross-border crime crackdown
items.summary: TUMPAT, Nov 3 — The Southeast Brigade of the General Operations Force (GOF) recorded 1,493 cross-border crime cases between Jan 1 and Nov 1, with enforcement operations resulting in 1,733 arrests and seizures worth more than RM82.56 million. Its commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the achievement demonstrated his personnel’s dedication and efficiency in carrying out enforcement duties aimed at safeguarding national security and sovereignty. He said GOF had strengthened its intelligence capabilities and heightened personnel awareness of emerging threats, particularly the use of alternative routes and hidden locations by cross-border criminals seeking to evade detection.

items.title: Russia strikes kill 26 in Ukraine, dealing fresh blow to peace hopes
items.summary: KYIV, Nov 3 — Ukraine said Monday that Russian strikes on a school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people, dashing fragile hopes of “progress toward peace” after a local ceasefire in the south expired without violations. Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said. “Every Monday, humanitarian aid was distributed to people there,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his daily address.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: Smart city solutions, bus hub among plans to ease Bukit Jalil concert traffic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traffic congestion in Bukit Jalil, particularly during concerts and large-scale events, has prompted the government to explore smart city solutions while refining traffic management plans to improve traffic flow in the area. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud had appointed consultants to conduct a Bukit Jalil micro-traffic management study, taking into account various issues raised by residents, including traffic congestion. She said the study was important as Bukit Jalil had unique characteristics as an event and concert hub that generated heavy traffic, requiring a specialised traffic management approach compared with other areas.

items.title: Over 8,500 postal ballots distributed for Melaka election, EC reminds voters on secrecy rules
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 3 — The Election Commission (EC) yesterday issued 8,569 postal ballot papers to eligible voters for the 16th Melaka State Election. EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said 8,041 of the postal ballot papers were issued to election officials, EC members and officers, police and military personnel, and media practitioners who had applied under Category 1A. Khairul Shahril reminded postal voters to mark their ballot papers and complete the Identity Declaration Form (Form 2) correctly before returning them to their respective constituency returning officers by 5 pm on polling day, Nov 14.

items.title: AirBorneo, Bintulu Port handover among key gains from Federal-Sarawak cooperation, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Strong cooperation and a close working relationship between the Federal Government and the Sarawak government have delivered high-impact transport development projects in the state within a short period, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. He said close cross-party cooperation with his deputy, Datuk Hasbi Habibollah, has allowed several major commitments to be fulfilled for the people of Sarawak. “For Sarawak, we have jointly delivered on several major matters at the Transport Ministry.

items.title: KTMB cargo train locomotive catches fire along Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang route, no injuries
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has confirmed that a cargo train locomotive caught fire at Kilometer 4.75 along the Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang route at about 1.10 pm yesterday. In a statement, KTMB said locomotive M1004 was hauling cargo train No. “The fire was completely extinguished by the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) at 2.50 pm.

items.title: MACC arrests Kedah policeman suspected of taking RM15,000 in bribes to protect drug trade
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 3 — The Kedah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) arrested a policeman suspected of soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000 from a drug trafficker two years ago. A MACC source said yesterday that the suspect is believed to have accepted bribes as an inducement to protect drug trafficking activities and prevent law enforcement action in the state. “Initial investigations revealed that the suspect is believed to have committed the acts throughout 2024,” the source said.

items.title: Ipoh police bust investment scam call centre targeting victims in Germany, five arrested
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 3 — Police arrested five Chinese nationals suspected of involvement in an investment scam syndicate during a raid on a house in Anjung Bercham Utama here last Friday. “Based on initial investigations and conversation scripts found on seized computers, police believe the syndicate ran a call centre operation to carry out non-existent online investment scams. Mohd Alwi said victims were persuaded to join investment schemes claimed to be based in Germany that promised high returns.

items.title: Ramanan: More than 500 houses affected by floods in Sungai Buloh, relief centre opened
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — More than 500 houses have been affected by floods following heavy rain in several areas around Sungai Buloh, Selangor, particularly Kampung Melayu Subang, yesterday. Sungai Buloh MP, Datuk Seri R Ramanan said the affected residents had been evacuated to a temporary relief centre opened at Dewan Siantan in Kampung Melayu Subang. “The centre will remain operational for as long as necessary to ensure that affected residents receive adequate shelter and assistance,” he posted on Facebook last night.

items.title: Malaysia has 10,036 patients with organ failure as Health Ministry pushes transplant reforms
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the need was increasingly urgent as the deceased-donor rate was 1.33 per million population. He said the establishment of the National Transplant Council (MTK) was a strategic step towards strengthening governance and driving the national organ donation agenda through a whole-of-government approach, replacing the fragmented efforts of individual agencies. Dzulkefly said he had chaired the first MTK meeting yesterday afternoon.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Pipeline project recovery, airport smuggling and delayed projects under scrutiny
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Efforts to recover payments made for the Trans-Sabah Gas Pipeline (TSGP) and Multi-Product Pipeline (MPP) projects, as well as tighter security at the country’s borders, are among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on Parliament’s official website, during Ministers’ Question Time, Datuk Jonathan Yasin (GRS-Ranau) will ask the Prime Minister about measures to recover payments for the TSGP and MPP projects, which reportedly received 88 per cent of their total payments, amounting to RM8.3 billion, despite being only 13 per cent complete. Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau) will seek an explanation from the Prime Minister on measures to strengthen border security and improve coordination among enforcement agencies following an increase in drug and contraband smuggling, particularly through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and Subang Airport.

items.title: Budget 2027: Fewer queues, simpler payments — what Malaysia’s digital government push means for you
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Fewer trips to government offices, less paperwork and simpler online payments could be on the cards for Malaysians as the government pushes ahead with a five-year plan to bring more public services online. Budget 2027 reinforces the push through initiatives including wider use of MyDigital ID, integrated government services and plans for a Sovereign AI Cloud. Will government services become easier to use?

items.title: Orang Asli village near KL still struggles with electricity despite solar projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — As the sun sets over Kampung Orang Asli Sg Relang, a devouring darkness comes with the stretching shadows, swallowing almost all sight and sound. Like at least 116 Orang Asli villages, according to government data in 2024, Kampung Sg Relang has mostly gone without electricity throughout the years. A view of Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang during a recent Bernama visit.

items.title: Pakatan files police report against BN’s Rim candidate over alleged use of govt assets in Melaka campaign, evidence to go to EC
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 2 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has lodged a police report against Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the 16th Melaka state election, Datuk Khaidirah Abu Zahar, over allegations that she campaigned using government premises and machinery. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Central Leadership Council (MPP) member Siti Aishah Shaik Ismail said the police report against the incumbent for Rim state constituency was filed by a PH representative at the Jasin district police headquarters (IPD) today. Aishah said they also possess evidence showing several MPJ officials wearing attire that displayed the face of the Jasin Umno vice-chief throughout the contribution distribution event.

items.title: Police free two on bail, track more suspects with Indonesia’s help in tanker ketamine case
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director, Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, said these individuals have been identified, and efforts to locate them are underway to assist with further investigations. “We recently arrested two individuals, but their remand period has since expired. Commenting on the case of a Chinese national detained at Hong Kong International Airport on suspicion of transporting two kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine from Penang, Hussein noted that the drug syndicate appears to have shifted away from using Malaysian citizens.

items.title: Investment, love and job scams: Nine locals among 141 arrested as Penang police bust 14 online call centres
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Penang police arrested 141 individuals, including nine locals, in 14 raids on call centres suspected of conducting various online scam operations in the state from October 9 to 29. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the state Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) operation involved five raids in Timur Laut district, six in Barat Daya district, and three in Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT), following intelligence gathering and surveillance. Lim said police also seized equipment, including mobile phones, laptops, tablets, internet routers, electronic equipment and computer accessories, believed to be used in the syndicates’ operations, valued at RM1.4 million.

items.title: Police rule out racial, gang links in Desa Tun Razak clash; seek 15 more suspects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police have ruled out racial and gang-related elements in an altercation involving a group of individuals outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, last night. Cheras police chief ACP Mohd Rosdi Daud said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a business turf dispute, although investigations were ongoing to establish the actual cause. Earlier, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that nine people had been arrested by a team from the Sungai Besi Police Station’s Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit and the Cheras district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division.

items.title: Police arrest man at Penang airport over RM3.2m cannabis bound for London; RM1.05m drugs seized in Jelutong
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Police arrested a local man in possession of 40 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds, valued at RM3.2 million, which were allegedly being smuggled to London. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the 28-year-old man, who hails from Miri, Sarawak, was apprehended at about 5pm while in the airport’s waiting area and the drugs were discovered during an inspection of his luggage. In a separate case, Lim said police arrested three individuals, including a Chinese national woman, during a raid at an apartment in Jelutong here yesterday evening.

items.title: Operasi Payung: Education Ministry boosts flood prep for SPM candidates, says deputy D-G
items.summary: Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation was aimed at helping candidates in flood-affected areas sit for their examinations without disruption. He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations. Zainal said the ministry was also coordinating preparations with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), state and district disaster management committees and other relevant agencies to assist areas at risk of flooding.

items.title: KL to get 22km of covered walkways under RM55m project starting Jan 2027, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Putrajaya will spend RM55 million to build the covered pedestrian walkways across the capital city, with the start of work scheduled for January 2027, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh told Parliament this evening. Under Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) operating expenditure, 22 kilometres of covered walkways will be built across Kuala Lumpur’s parliamentary constituencies, with an allocation of two kilometres per constituency, she said. Yeoh said the walkways are designed to bridge critical urban gaps by connecting residential zones, public facilities, commercial hubs, bus stops, health clinics and places of worship.

items.title: Demand for ETS, EMUPlus tickets for Deepavali exceeds offered capacity as 100,304 tickets sold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has recorded the sale of 100,304 tickets for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and EMUPlus services for the Deepavali period, covering travel dates from November 5 to November 10. KTMB group chief executive officer Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the high demand reflects a positive public response to the rail services during the festive season. KTMB had previously announced an additional 14,384 seats across its ETS and EMUPlus services to meet passenger demand for the festival.

items.title: Border control agency DG Shuhaily returns to duty after leave
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 2 — The director-general of the Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, resumed his duties at the agency today, following reports that he had been on leave last week. In a post on its official Facebook page, AKPS said Mohd Shuhaily began his duties by chairing the ‘Commander’s Call’ Meeting No. Those present included AKPS deputy director-general (operations), Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M Nasir; AKPS deputy director-general (policy), Zuraini Othman; and AKPS Commander for Port Klang, Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.
